title: ChatGPT just blocked its most controversial writing feature
excerpt: There are already complaints that changes to the paid subscription are ruining writing for some users.
content_html:
Published Jul 28, 2026, 4:43 PM EDT

Will has almost seven years of experience writing about technology and its wider impacts.  His work has appeared in The New York Times, BBC News, The Guardian, The Times of London, The Daily Beast, Vice, Slate, Fast Company, The Evening Standard, The i, TechRadar, and Decrypt Media.

He has covered everything from crypto scandals to the art world, as well as conspiracy theories, UK politics, and Russia and foreign affairs.

Summary

  • ChatGPT now refuses prompts to mimic specific named authors.
  • The move is likely spurred by big copyright settlements and author lawsuits.
  • Claude and Gemini still comply; users can describe author traits instead.

OpenAI's ChatGPT will no longer carry out prompts that request that the chatbot mimic a particular author's style.

As reported by Ars Technica, ChatGPT has begun rejecting requests to generate text in the style of living authors like Stephen King or dead authors like Charles Dickens and Ernest Hemingway. Though the chatbot refused to directly comply, it did offer to write something "with the hallmarks of atmospheric, character-driven horror and small-town dread," showing it could still imitate some elements of an author's work.

Reddit users have already noticed the change, with some complaining that they had paid for a subscription and that it was ruining their book-writing process.

OpenAI hasn't officially announced the change or explained the reasoning behind the move — but Anthropic's recent copyright lawsuit settlement may well have pushed the artificial intelligence company to act now.

ChatGPT won't write like Dickens any more

It's throwing a spanner in literary works

AI-generated writing, whether people like it or not, isn't just clogging up your LinkedIn or Amazon reviews; it's wormed its way into the world of professional fiction.

Bestselling books have now been hit with accusations of being, at least in part, AI-generated, while prestigious literary magazines have been accused of publishing AI-generated stories. Many organizations, including the Authors Guild, are suing OpenAI (OpenClassAction), with famous authors like John Grisham and Game of Thrones writer George R.R. Martin alleging the AI giant is profiting off their copyrighted work.

Anthropic, the company behind Claude, recently agreed to pay out $1.5 billion to a group of authors following a class-action lawsuit, which accused the company of using their work to train its chatbot. It was the largest copyright settlement in US history, and it's likely this enormous lawsuit that's prompting OpenAI to reconsider how its chatbot delivers literary advice.

These types of imitation mechanics were obviously being widely used. As Futurism highlights, one romance author accidentally revealed that they had asked a chatbot to rewrite a paragraph in the style of J. Bree, a popular author in their genre, in one of their books published earlier this year.

“I’ve rewritten the passage to align more with J. Bree’s style, which features more tension, gritty undertones, and raw emotional subtext beneath the supernatural elements,” read a passage from the book.

Claude and Gemini will still comply for now

According to users on Reddit, both Anthropic's Claude and Google Gemini will still comply with users' requests to create text in the style of living authors. When we tested it, both chatbots explained that they would follow copyright rules and wouldn't produce verbatim text taken from the author's work.

Redditors also recommended manually describing the style of the author you want to emulate, rather than giving a name, to work around the restriction.

  • 这一举措可能是受到大规模版权和解和作者诉讼的推动。

OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 将不再执行要求聊天机器人模仿特定作者风格的提示。

据 Ars Technica 报道，ChatGPT 已开始拒绝以斯蒂芬·金等在世作家或查尔斯·狄更斯和欧内斯特·海明威等已故作家的风格生成文本的请求。 尽管聊天机器人拒绝直接遵守，但它确实提出写一些“具有大气、角色驱动的恐怖和小镇恐惧的标志”的东西，这表明它仍然可以模仿作者作品的某些元素。

Reddit 用户已经注意到了这一变化，一些人抱怨说他们已经付费订阅了，这破坏了他们的写书过程。

OpenAI 尚未正式宣布这一变化，也没有解释此举背后的原因，但 Anthropic 最近的版权诉讼和解很可能促使这家人工智能公司立即采取行动。

ChatGPT 不会再像狄更斯那样写作

它给文学作品带来了麻烦

人工智能生成的写作，无论人们喜欢与否，不仅会堵塞你的 LinkedIn 或亚马逊评论，还会堵塞你的评论。它已经进入了职业小说的世界。

畅销书现在受到至少部分由人工智能生成的指控，而著名的文学杂志也被指控出版人工智能生成的故事。 包括作家协会在内的许多组织正在起诉 OpenAI (OpenClassAction)，其中包括约翰·格里沙姆 (John Grisham) 和《权力的游戏》编剧乔治·R·R·乔治 (George R.R. 马丁声称这家人工智能巨头正在从他们的版权作品中获利。

Claude 背后的公司 Anthropic 最近同意向一群作者支付 15 亿美元，此前该公司发起集体诉讼，指控该公司利用他们的作品来训练其聊天机器人。 这是美国历史上最大的版权和解协议，这场巨大的诉讼很可能促使 OpenAI 重新考虑其聊天机器人如何提供文学建议。

这些类型的模仿机械显然被广泛使用。 正如《未来主义》所强调的那样，一位浪漫主义作家无意中透露，他们已要求聊天机器人以 J. 的风格重写一个段落。 布莉（Bree）是该类型中的一位受欢迎的作家，在他们今年早些时候出版的一本书中。

“我重写了这段话，以便与 J 更加一致。 布莉的风格在超自然元素之下具有更多的张力、坚韧的基调和原始的情感潜台词，”书中的一段话这样写道。

克劳德和双子座暂时还是会遵守

Reddit 上的用户表示，Anthropic 的 Claude 和 Google Gemini 仍将遵守用户的要求，以在世作家的风格创建文本。 当我们测试它时，两个聊天机器人都解释说它们将遵循版权规则，并且不会生成从作者作品中获取的逐字文本。

Reddit 用户还建议手动描述您想要模仿的作者的风格，而不是给出名字，以解决该限制。
